title: Protocols for Preparation of Blood Smears and Reporting of Malaria Parasites
author: Kwame Agyemang Adusei
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.prydm7w

steps.title: Prepare Thick Blood Smear
steps.instruction: Prepare a thick blood smear on a clean grease-free slide.

substeps.instruction: Place a drop of well mixed blood (6ul) on a clean grease-free slide using a pipette.
Use an applicator to spread the blood in a circular motion to a moderate thickness, covering an area of approximately 1cm diameter.
Label the slide with the subject's code number and allow to air-dry.

steps.title: Stain Thick Smear
steps.instruction: Stain the thick smear using Giemsa stain.

substeps.instruction: Stain the smear with freshly prepared 10% Giemsa stain for 15 minutes.
Wash with clean distilled water.
Place slides on a drying rack in a vertical position and allow to air dry.

steps.title: Prepare Thin Blood Smear
steps.instruction: Prepare a thin blood smear using the spreader slide technique.

substeps.instruction: Place a drop of well mixed blood (2ul) approximately 1cm from the frosted end of a slide using a pipette.
Place the smooth clean edge of a second slide (spreader) in front of the blood drop.
Hold the spreader slide at a 30° angle and draw it back against the blood drop.
As blood spreads to the ends of the spreader, push the spreader forward with a light, smooth, and quick steady motion.
Label the frosted edge with the subject's code number.

steps.title: Fix and Stain Thin Smear
steps.instruction: Fix and stain the thin smear.

substeps.instruction: Dip the smear in a Coplin jar containing absolute methanol for 10 seconds and air dry.
Stain with freshly prepared Giemsa stain solution for 30 minutes.
Wash with distilled water and place on a drying rack to air dry.

steps.title: Examine Slides Microscopically
steps.instruction: Examine the prepared films under oil immersion to identify malaria parasites.

substeps.instruction: Examine the thick film using the X100 objective lens with oil immersion.
Examine the thin film first using the X40 objective lens with oil immersion at the feathery tip to check staining, morphology, and cell distribution.
Switch to the X100 objective lens to examine malaria parasites.

steps.title: Quantify Parasite Density
steps.instruction: Calculate the number of parasites per microliter of blood.

substeps.instruction: Count all parasite species and forms (sexual and asexual) in 100 fields.
Count 200 white blood cells (WBCs) in relation to the parasites, using an average of 8000/µl as the standard WBC count.
Calculate density using the formula: NUMBER OF PARASITES/µL = (Number of parasites counted / Number of white blood cells counted) × 8000.

steps.title: Perform Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT)
steps.instruction: Conduct an RDT for malaria detection.

substeps.instruction: Take 5ul of whole blood from a labeled EDTA tube using the provided pipette.
Pipette the blood into the round sample well of the RDT.
Place four drops of assay diluent vertically into the square assay diluent well.
Read results after 30 minutes: a positive result shows both test and control bands; a negative result shows only the control band.

steps.title: Determine Blood Group via Tile Method
steps.instruction: Use the forward grouping tile method to determine blood groups.

substeps.instruction: Place 5ul of blood sample into the appropriate square of the tile.
Add a drop of known antisera to the sample.
Mix with an applicator and rock the tile forward and backward for 3 minutes.
Read results macroscopically upon agglutination, or microscopically if results are unclear.
